- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot true values, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model underreacts to sustained downward trends; true values often dip below forecasted levels after a period of high prices.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — forecasts show less tendency to return to historical averages than actual data.
- Forecast accuracy improves when model adjusts downward after a 3–5 day spike, but often lags by 1–3 days.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting overconfidence in upward momentum.
- When history shows strong volatility, forecasts tend to smooth out extremes too much, missing sharp reversals.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–3% for each day after a price spike exceeding 2% above the 30-day moving average.
